output.brief: The wrong expiry dates came from bad data, not from operators or the printer upgrade. On 3 Oct Regulatory Affairs entered a 36-month shelf life for Veltranol, valid from March 2027, and left the current 24 months in place. From 4 Oct the data sent to the printers carried 36 months. Every job after that printed expiry 12 months late. That includes two day-shift jobs on Line 1 run by permanent staff. 30 earlier jobs, including agency-operator and post-firmware jobs, were correct. No operator overrides occurred, and the camera only compares the print to the job, so it passed everything. The vendor says future-dated values can't be sent, but the logs show one was. Why that happened is still open. Please check it with the vendor and IT. Don't discipline the agency staff, and don't switch off the camera check. Do this next. Fix the Veltranol shelf-life record. Hold every Veltranol lot packed since 4 Oct, including the two in the warehouse. Add a second-person check of printed expiry against the batch record at each setup. Inspect retained cartons of the other products edited in October, especially the two with future-dated changes. Wider reconciliation and relabelling should wait for those results. I'm fairly confident in the main cause. Whether other products are affected is unknown.
